title: The Utility Monster
summary: Imagine a creature that gets enormously more happiness from every resource than anyone else does. If the right thing to do is whatever produces the most happiness in total, we should give everything to the monster, even if everyone else is left with nothing. Robert Nozick raised the case in 1974 as a problem for utilitarian theories that simply add up well-being, because it seems to show that such adding ignores how happiness is shared between people.
citations: Robert Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (Basic Books, 1974), p. 41
Walter Sinnott-Armstrong, "Consequentialism," Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/consequentialism/
